title: Travel Across the Nation
text:
Lincoln Memorial
NOTES / OBSERVATIONS

Traveling to the other side of the country expands your perspective on American politics. Visiting the Lincoln memorial at night and witnessing its sheer enormity reminds me of the foundational democratic ideals of the U.S. government.

title: Travel Across the Nation
text:
What I want to remember

The immense scale of the monument serves as a physical reminder to zoom out and look at the bigger picture of America’s democracy, especially given the current climate of political polarization.

title: What a chart can tell me
text: A chart makes some patterns easier to see, but it also reflects a series of choices. Which observations belong in the plot? What belongs on each axis? Which differences deserve attention?

title: What a chart can tell me
text:
One choice that matters
In a comparison of income and life expectancy, a logarithmic income axis changes the spacing of the values. That can help reveal patterns that are difficult to see when a few large values stretch the scale.

title: What a chart can tell me
section: What I still need to ask
text:
What I still need to ask
A visible association does not explain why the pattern exists. Before moving from description to explanation, I need to think about the research question, the data, and possible alternative explanations.
My next step is to describe the plot in one careful sentence, then write down a question it cannot answer.

title: Profession & Career
text:
Experience & Research

Student Researcher · Empirical Approaches Course Project
FALL 2025
Project: Exploring Gun Control Across the United States (with J. Villasenor)

Investigated how state-level citizen ideology and institutional government quality affect the gun control laws that are passed.
Conducted a literature review on how political parties, trust in government, and identity shape what voters care about.
Shifted research from personal opinions toward clear measures of administrative competence to understand how policy outcomes differ across states.
Used official interest group ratings of politicians to analyze state political contexts rather than relying on survey data.

title: Academic interests & research
text:
As a political science major, I am interested in gun control, which has become an increasingly divisive partisan issue in the United States.

Gun violence and gun regulation How do state-level variations in citizen political ideology shape gun control legislation and the threat of gun violence in the U.S.?
Law and public policy: How does state-level institutional capacity (government quality and administrative competence) moderate the relationship between ideological preferences and the actual enforcement of gun control laws?
Data and communication: What are the structural limitations and gaps between understanding citizen preferences and actual policy outcomes?

title: Academic interests & research
text:
A project I’m developing

Exploring gun control across the United States
COURSE PROJECT · IN PROGRESS
Research Question. How does state-level citizen ideology influence gun control laws across the U.S.?
Approach. Use R to conduct a state-level analysis of gun control to examine the relationship between citizen ideology, state gun control laws, and government quality.
What I’m learning. Running cross-tabulation analyses to discover the association between partisan gun control attitudes and the strength of gun laws, as well as the moderating effect of government quality on this relationship.

Read the full study here: Gun Violence.

title: Academic interests & research
text:
Looking forward
I plan to explore the topic further by analyzing whether gun regulations are effectively implemented and enforced, rather than simply whether strict laws exist, which would better explain the role of government quality in the relationship between ideology and gun policy.
